prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Bellroy (company_id bellroy; category: wallets, bags and carry goods)
Official domains: bellroy.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://bellroy.com/journal/a-letter-from-our-co-founders | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Now engineer, co-founder and Bellroy's CEO, Lina, remembers what happened from there... We wanted to build both a great brand and a great business. The kind that could really delight its customers, not just satisfy them. We wanted deep relationships with our partners, where we could invest in finding better ways, together. We wanted to work with great people who cared about shaping a better world. We launched Bellroy with a very tight range of five wallets, and a hardworking team of five people. While so many parts of the business needed to be developed, our customers quickly started telling us that they loved what we were doing. And that was the most important reason to keep going."

[P2] source: https://bellroy.com/journal/celebrating-ten-years | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"We were Made for Google. Since the beginning, we’d been designing products to enhance our customers’ everyday experiences. And it’s fair to say we were pretty thrilled when a small, unknown Silicon Valley brand by the name of Google (sarcasm alert) asked us to do the same for their products. The first Made for Google collection launched with a leather case for Pixel, a sleeve for the Pixelbook and a Pixelbook pen clip."

[P3] source: https://bellroy.com/responsible-business | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"By making products that are used and loved for as long as possible. * * Our products are designed to feel better on day 1000 than on day one. And hold what can be known as ‘emotional durability’. * By making sure our products are available where our customers need them. * * We ship directly to 187 countries around the world, translate our content into seven languages and partner with approximately 1000 retailers globally. 2."

[P4] source: https://bellroy.com/responsible-business | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"By ensuring good – not just fair – conditions for all of our suppliers and factory workers. * * Our supplier Code of Conduct and audit process ensures that Bellroy's suppliers provide safe working conditions, that their workers are treated with respect and dignity, and that the manufacturing processes are environmentally responsible. * By aligning with professional organizations who share our values. * * This includes our suppliers, retailers and brand partners, to not only achieve the first objective of the partnership, but actively work together to improve how we both do things."

[P5] source: https://bellroy.com/journal/celebrating-ten-years | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Slim Your Wallet became a thing. Fast. We soon started to see that the world had been ready and waiting for slim wallets. So we doubled down, registered slimyourwallet.com and launched a campaign that we’re still known for today."

[P6] source: https://bellroy.com/journal/celebrating-ten-years | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2017 | published: unknown
"The time for hiding in pockets was officially over. We launched bags! Bellroy was always intended to be a bag brand… but in true Bellroy style, we took a few years to get our bag designs into the world. After bedding down customer insights and design tricks gathered over the years, we felt ready and able to make a difference to the way bags were designed and made. So in late 2017, we released our first collection of six styles. Including our ever-popular staple, the Classic Backpack."

[P7] source: https://www.drip.com/blog/bellroy-marketing | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"(Note the dual branding on the wallet). Huckberry Hide and Seek Huckberry’s collaboration with Bellroy was so successful that they now sell Bellroy products on their site, permanently. Bellroy on Huckberry What started as a one-time collaboration became a long-term partnership benefiting both brands. More recently, Bellroy partnered with Google to develop a sleeve for Google’s Pixelbook. Bellroy_s Pixelbook Sleeve The best part? Not only was it good social proof for Bellroy, they also got a TON of free press from several authority review blogs. Bellroy in Google News Even better, they got a nice do-follow link from the Google Store."

[P8] source: https://bellroy.com/responsible-business | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"By integrating our partners with purpose, to develop better business practices, supply chain processes and working conditions together. 3."

[P9] source: https://bellroy.com/press | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"We collaborate We’re proud to have worked with some talented brands, including Google, Field Notes, Barneys New York, MAAP and Huckberry."

[P10] source: https://bellroy.com/journal/a-letter-from-our-co-founders | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: 2010, 2015, 2020 | published: unknown
"By 2015, with our wallet range now mostly bedded down, we were ready to start chasing our dream of addressing other areas within carry. When we look at Bellroy in 2020, it’s a remarkably different brand to when we sold our first wallet in 2010. And yet so many of our values and approaches have remained, and continue to be critical to our DNA. There are now hundreds of people who work on Bellroy. We offer a broad range of carry products that help people get more out of their everyday – day after day, year after year. We’ve pleased millions of customers with designs that broke existing conventions. And all while channeling resources and funds towards helping shape a better world."

generator.quote_repair: claims.repair_quotes (min similarity 0.9; numbers/negations unchanged); see attempts[].quote_repairs
